name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Republican win at 99%
Chuck Gray's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this seat effectively unwinnable for Democrats, and markets price a Republican win at 99%. Gray holds a massive financial and outside-spending advantage over a Democratic opponent who has raised under $20,000, so the forecast sits slightly beyond the state's baseline lean.
model.watch: A major scandal or an unexpectedly strong Libertarian/Constitutionalist showing could shave a few points off Gray's margin, but not the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-held in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+23. Harriet Hageman is leaving the seat to run for Senate, and Chuck Gray enters the general as the heavy favorite after a well-funded primary campaign. He has raised about $1.6 million and drawn over $1.6 million in outside support, while Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 with essentially no cash on hand.

Prediction markets put the Republican's chances at 99%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling and a thin Democratic operation, the main question is the size of Gray's victory margin rather than the winner. A Libertarian and a Constitutionalist candidate are also on the ballot but are unlikely to alter the result materially.
